topics.justification: Top words like "expire", "date", "valid", "revocation/revoke", "compromise" and "year/day" indicate discussions about certificate validity periods and what to do when keys are compromised or certs must be revoked.
The dominance of "file", "window", "click", "select", "install/instal", "download", and "directory/path" suggests procedural guidance for adding certificates via Windows UI/tools.

topics.topic_name: Browser trust, domain matching & HTTPS warnings
topics.justification: Words such as "browser", "site/website", "domain", "trust", "warning", "dns" and "match" point to certificate errors in browsers (e.g., name mismatch, untrusted CA) and how trust is established for domains.

topics.topic_name: OpenSSL certificate/CSR generation and signing commands
topics.justification: "openssl", "command", "option", "generate", "request", "self_sign_certificate" and "sign_certificate" strongly indicate command-line OpenSSL workflows for creating keys, CSRs, and issuing/signing certificates.

Terms like "public_key", "private_key", "encrypt/encryption", "signature", "hash", "encode", and "byte/string" reflect implementation-level questions about performing cryptographic operations using keys and certificate-contained public keys.

High weights for "server", "client", "connection/connect", "request/send/receive", "verify", and "authentication" indicate questions about how certificates are exchanged and validated in TLS connections (including fingerprints).

topics.topic_name: Code signing and signature verification (incl. timestamping)
topics.justification: "code", "sign/signing", "digital_signature", "verify", "release/build", and "timestamp" align with signing executables/documents, verifying integrity, and preserving trust over time via timestamps.

topics.topic_name: PKCS#11 / HSM-backed key access in applications
topics.justification: The presence of "pkcs11", alongside "library", "tool", "service", "application", and "access" suggests integrating apps with hardware tokens/HSMs or smartcards via PKCS#11 for key operations.

Keywords "private_key", "keystore", "password", "format", "import/export", "convert", "pkcs12" and "openssl" indicate handling and migrating key material between files/keystores (e.g., PFX/PKCS#12) securely.

"extension", "field", "subject", "attribute", "usage", and "policy" point to how certificate metadata is structured and what extensions/attributes must be included to meet specific validation requirements.

Frequent "error", "fail", "exception", "message", "method", "return", "test", and "verify" suggests posts focused on troubleshooting implementation mistakes and runtime failures in certificate or signature validation code.

topics.topic_name: Trust stores and certificate chain building/validation
topics.justification: Strong signals from "trust", "store", "root", "chain", "certificate_chain", "trust_root", "validate/verify", and "add" indicate managing root CAs and verifying full chains against system/application trust stores.
